label: Data Movement: Table Types and Data Operations
topic: Data Movement: external, Iceberg and hybrid tables, schema evolution, unload

questions.scenario: A Data Engineer owns an external table over Parquet files in an S3 bucket. The table was created with AUTO_REFRESH = TRUE, and the bucket event notification points to the SQS queue ARN shown in the notification_channel column of SHOW EXTERNAL TABLES. New files appeared in queries within a minute until last week. Then a security change moved the table's database to a new role with GRANT OWNERSHIP ... COPY CURRENT GRANTS. The event notification on the bucket has not been edited, and the SQS ARN has not changed. Files added since the change do not appear, although manual refreshes show them.
questions.stem: Which action restores automatic registration of new files?

options.text: Set AWS_SNS_TOPIC on the external table to the ARN of an SNS topic that receives the bucket events
Run ALTER EXTERNAL TABLE ... REFRESH once, which registers the current files and re-enables event-driven registration
Run ALTER EXTERNAL TABLE ... SET AUTO_REFRESH = TRUE as the new owner
Delete the bucket event notification and recreate it with the ARN from the notification_channel column

explanation.correct: Transferring ownership of an external table, or of its parent database, with GRANT OWNERSHIP sets AUTO_REFRESH to FALSE. The notification setup is still valid, so setting AUTO_REFRESH back to TRUE with ALTER EXTERNAL TABLE restores event-driven registration.

distractors.A: AWS_SNS_TOPIC applies only when S3 events are routed through an SNS topic. The existing SQS notification still works, and the cause is the AUTO_REFRESH setting.
distractors.B: A manual REFRESH registers the files that exist at that moment. It does not change AUTO_REFRESH, so later files would again go unregistered.
distractors.D: The SQS queue ARN has not changed, so the existing event notification is still correct. Recreating it does not change the AUTO_REFRESH value that was reset.

questions.scenario: A Data Engineer keeps an external table over S3 files whose partitions are also registered in an AWS Glue catalog. The table was created with PARTITION_TYPE = USER_SPECIFIED. A new path, dt=2026-11-25, arrives each day, and queries do not return its rows.
questions.stem: Which statement makes the new day's files queryable?

options.text: Run ALTER EXTERNAL TABLE ... REFRESH '<path>' so that Snowflake registers the files of the new partition
Set AUTO_REFRESH = TRUE on the table so that event notifications register the files of the new partition
Run ALTER EXTERNAL TABLE ... ADD FILES for the files in the new path so that they are registered one by one
Run ALTER EXTERNAL TABLE ... ADD PARTITION (dt = '2026-11-25') LOCATION 'dt=2026-11-25' for the new path

explanation.correct: With USER_SPECIFIED partitions, partitions are added with ALTER EXTERNAL TABLE ... ADD PARTITION and removed with DROP PARTITION LOCATION.

distractors.A: REFRESH is not supported on a table with user-specified partitions. A manual refresh raises a user error.
distractors.B: AUTO_REFRESH is not supported for PARTITION_TYPE = USER_SPECIFIED.
distractors.C: ADD FILES and REMOVE FILES are not supported on a table with user-specified partitions.

questions.scenario: A bucket holds about 5 million Parquet files under dated prefixes. A Data Engineer runs CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE with the default settings, and the statement takes very long because it refreshes the metadata for all of the files.
questions.stem: Which approach registers all of the files without relying on one very long statement?

options.text: Create the table with REFRESH_ON_CREATE = FALSE, then run ALTER EXTERNAL TABLE ... REFRESH per sub-path
Create the table with AUTO_REFRESH = FALSE only, because the refresh at creation depends on that setting
Name the individual files in the LOCATION clause so that Snowflake registers only the files that are listed
Copy the files to an internal stage and create the external table on that stage for faster registration

explanation.correct: With about a million files or more, REFRESH_ON_CREATE = FALSE skips the refresh at creation. Refreshing one relative sub-path at a time with ALTER EXTERNAL TABLE ... REFRESH then registers all of the files.

distractors.B: REFRESH_ON_CREATE is a separate setting and defaults to TRUE, so the refresh at creation still runs.
distractors.C: LOCATION cannot name individual files. PATTERN is the way to filter by file name.
distractors.D: External tables are not supported on internal stages.

questions.scenario: An external table points at S3 files stored under 2026/11/25/ style prefixes. The table has only the VALUE column. Queries filter with WHERE value:event_date::DATE = '2026-11-25', and every query scans all of the files.
questions.stem: Which change reduces the files that are scanned?

options.text: Add a clustering key on the event date column of the external table so that files are grouped by date
Increase the size of the warehouse so that the scan of all of the files finishes sooner
Recreate the table with a partition column derived from METADATA$FILENAME, and filter on that column
Move the date filter into the WHERE clause on the VALUE column so that file pruning applies to it

explanation.correct: External tables prune files with partition columns, which are defined with PARTITION BY and an expression over METADATA$FILENAME. The partition method cannot be changed after creation, so the table is recreated, and queries must filter on the partition column.

distractors.A: Clustering keys are not supported on external tables.
distractors.B: A larger warehouse scans the same files faster, but it does not reduce the files that are scanned.
distractors.D: A filter on the VALUE column does not prune files. Only filters on partition columns do.

questions.scenario: A finance analyst sees credits for external table auto-refresh across 30 external tables on S3. The Data Engineer needs, for each table, the files that were registered and the credits that auto-refresh used.

options.text: WAREHOUSE_METERING_HISTORY, because auto-refresh runs on the warehouse that last queried each table
AUTO_REFRESH_REGISTRATION_HISTORY, which needs ACCOUNTADMIN or the MONITOR USAGE privilege
COPY_HISTORY, because each registered file is loaded into the external table like a COPY
QUERY_HISTORY, because each auto-refresh appears as a query with its own credits used

explanation.correct: AUTO_REFRESH_REGISTRATION_HISTORY shows the files that were registered and the credits used by auto-refresh. It needs ACCOUNTADMIN or MONITOR USAGE.

distractors.A: Auto-refresh overhead is billed as Snowpipe charges, not as warehouse credits.
distractors.C: An external table does not load files. It registers file metadata, so nothing is loaded by COPY.
distractors.D: Auto-refresh overhead is billed as Snowpipe charges, so it is not tracked as the credits of a query.

questions.scenario: A Data Engineer must create an external table over a Delta Lake table in S3 with TABLE_FORMAT = DELTA. The Delta table receives new commits every hour.

options.text: Set REFRESH_ON_CREATE = FALSE and AUTO_REFRESH = FALSE, then refresh the table manually
Set AUTO_REFRESH = FALSE only, because a refresh at creation is allowed for Delta tables
Keep the defaults and add AWS_SNS_TOPIC so that new Delta commits are registered by event
Set both options to FALSE and refresh with a relative path so that only new log files are read

explanation.correct: A Delta Lake external table needs both REFRESH_ON_CREATE and AUTO_REFRESH set to FALSE, and it is refreshed manually. A manual refresh of a Delta external table uses a warehouse.

distractors.B: Both REFRESH_ON_CREATE and AUTO_REFRESH must be FALSE for Delta tables.
distractors.C: AUTO_REFRESH is not supported for Delta Lake external tables, so event notifications do not register Delta commits.
distractors.D: A relative path on REFRESH is not supported for Delta Lake external tables.

questions.scenario: A team plans to expose Parquet files in an S3 bucket as an external table and checks which table features and storage options it can rely on. Some of the objects are in the S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage class.
questions.stem: Which THREE statements are correct? (Select THREE.)

options.text: A clustering key can be added to the table to group rows from the same file
A row access policy can be attached to the table with ON (VALUE)
Constraints such as NOT NULL are defined but not enforced on the table
The table can be cloned to give developers their own copy to work on
Objects that need restoration from Glacier Deep Archive cannot be read
The LOCATION of the table can be an internal named stage in Snowflake

explanation.correct: Row access policies and masking policies work on external tables. Integrity constraints, including NOT NULL, are not enforced. Archive-tier objects that need restoration, such as S3 Glacier Deep Archive, cannot be used.

distractors.A: Clustering keys are not supported on external tables.
distractors.D: Cloning is not supported on external tables.
distractors.F: An external table reads files in an external stage. Internal stages are not supported.

questions.scenario: The role ANALYST_RO must query an external table. It already holds USAGE on the database, the schema and the file format, and SELECT on the table. A query still fails with an error that the stage is not accessible to the role.
questions.stem: Which TWO grants are needed to fix the error? (Select TWO.)

options.text: WRITE on the named stage that the table uses as its LOCATION
USAGE on the named stage that the table uses as its LOCATION
OWNERSHIP on the external table so that the role can read it
READ on the named stage that the table uses as its LOCATION
OPERATE on the external table so that the role can read it

explanation.correct: A role that is not the owner needs USAGE on the database, schema and file format, USAGE and READ on the named stage, and SELECT on the table.

distractors.A: WRITE on the stage is not needed to read an external table, which is read-only.
distractors.C: OWNERSHIP is needed to run ALTER EXTERNAL TABLE, for example to refresh it, and not to query it.
distractors.E: OPERATE is not one of the privileges that querying an external table requires.
